newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia satisfied with extent of property curbs.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia satisfied with extent of property curbs.

text.p: Malaysia is satisfied with the extent of curbs on property loans proposed late last month by the country's central bank, Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said in an interview aired on Monday.

"Right now, we are quite comfortable with the figures," Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, told Reuters Financial Television. "I don't see any need for the present to take undue or tougher measures because it is working."
In its 1996 annual report released on March 28, Bank Negara Malaysia said it will limit to 20 percent a bank's outstanding loans to the property sector from April 1.
Loans to the property sector had reached 30 percent of all commercial loans, the central bank said.
"I think the measures have been realistic," Anwar said in the interview. "We've taken into consideration the macroeconomic factors and issues at hand, and we will continue to monitor this."
He said the move by the central bank was "pre-emptive".

The Malaysian stock market has received the news of the property loan curbs badly. Property and banking shares were hit last week by concerns that their earnings growth would be impeded by the measures.
Bank Negara has been holding a few rounds of talks with bankers to discuss the guidelines since announcing them.
